item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Oct 24, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: National Make a Difference Day Tree Planting at LAMRC — Sat Oct 24, 9:00 AM — 5800 Chiles Road
item.description: Join CAL FIRE staff, affiliated organizations, and neighborhood residents and leaders as the Lewis A. Moran Reforestation Center (LAMRC) continues its green transformation and celebrates the site’s 105th anniversary! With support from West Coast Arborists, Tree Davis, and a volunteer Tree Advisory Group, we hope to welcome your help in reforesting the Reforestation Center with a palette of primarily climate-adapted trees for the Sacramento Valley. This event is being held on Saturday, October 24th from 9am-noon as part of National Make a Difference Day. Hear guest speakers detail the project and its trees, acknowledge the history of the site, and recognize the grander importance of making a difference in our community with future resilience in mind. Afterward, a tree-planting demonstration will be given before volunteers can assist with installing 15-gallon-sized specimens along the property’s perimeter. item.title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge — Sat Oct 24, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Sat Oct 24, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Birds & Bikes — Sat Oct 24, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. item.title: Un-Coding AI in the Classroom: 2-Day Workshop for Faculty and Instructors — Thu Dec 10 — DataLab Classroom
item.description:
Generative AI is reshaping the landscape of higher education, raising important questions for teaching, learning, and academic integrity. Designed for faculty and instructors across all disciplines and requiring no prior technical background, this two-day workshop unpacks genAI and offers practical strategies for the university classroom. Whether you are curious about how these models work, eager to integrate AI into your teaching, or cautious about its impact on student learning, this series offers a supportive, nuanced space to explore. Participants will gain a clear foundational understanding of large language models (LLMs), evaluate the opportunities and limitations of genAI, and engage in hands-on practice configuring customized and privacy-protected AI learning environments for their courses.
The workshop runs Thursday-Friday December 10-11 from 9 AM - 4 PM daily with a break for lunch. Full participation in both days is recommended as topics build across sessions.

item.title: Freedom of Expression at UC Davis: Know Your Rights — Tue Nov 24, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Ever wondered where the line is between free speech, campus policy, and taking a stand? Whether you're planning a demonstration, organizing an event with your RSO, or just navigating lively debates around campus, knowing your rightsis key.
Join CSI's Assistant Director for Student Expression, Jose Napoles, for an interactive breakdown of what Freedom of Expression actually looks like on campus. We’ll clear up the confusion around campus forums, break down time, place, and manner policies, and give you the tools to make informed decisions and keep your communities safe.

item.title: Honkai: Star Rail × Currency Wars: Random Challenge! — Fri Oct 23, 6:00 PM — Walker Hall
item.description:
Currency Wars – Random Challenge! Are you confident in your strategies and team-building skills in Honkai: Star Rail? Come and challenge yourself in the Currency Wars – Random Challenge! During the competition, participants will randomly draw special rules that restrict character selection, equipment, and battle strategies. Players must adjust their teams and overcome these unexpected challenges to achieve victory! The event also features Team Composition Rules and Fun Punishment Challenges, adding more excitement and surprises! After defeating each major boss, participants must complete a new fun challenge, such as singing, imitating characters, or performing funny actions. The player who completes the challenge in the shortest time while following all the rules wins! Are you ready to test your luck, creativity, and strategy? Join us and become the ultimate Currency Wars Master!
Source: UC Davis CampusGroups

item.title: Davis Farmers Market – Wednesday Evenings (50th Anniversary Year) — Wed Jan 6, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
The Davis Farmers Market continues every Wednesday in Central Park with new fall hours! Beginning Wednesday, September 2, the Wednesday market will be open from 3:00–6:00 PM, replacing the extended 4:00–8:00 PM Picnic in the Park hours. Stop by to shop for fresh, locally grown produce, artisan goods, prepared foods and other market favorites from local farmers and vendors. It’s a great opportunity to stock up for the week, meet up with friends, support local growers and food makers, and enjoy a beautiful afternoon in Central Park. The Davis Farmers Market is celebrating its 50th Anniversary in 2026, marking five decades of bringing fresh food, local farmers and the Davis community together. Wednesday Market Details:
Wednesdays from 3:00–6:00 PM Central Park in Downtown Davis Fresh, seasonal produce Artisan goods and prepared foods Local farmers and food makers Family-friendly and open to everyone

item.title: Blood on the Clocktower at Blue Note — Wed Jan 6, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering The first Wednesday of every month, we play _Blood on the Clocktower_, a social deduction game in the vein of Werewolf/Mafia/The Resistance, with a few twists!
We'll have a circle of chairs reserved inside Blue Note, near the back, with a Yolo County Board Game Gathering sign on the table. Just say hello, and we'll show you some games, pull some players together, and get to having fun!
We also usually have a few tables of players playing other board games, if social deduction isn't your bag!
Get a feel for Blood on the Clocktower here: https://youtu.be/4sfa8_kNxsQ
Source: Meetup: Yolo Board Game Gathering
